⚡️ Leader appoints Gen. Vahidi as IRGC chief commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei has appointed Brigadier General Ahmad Vahidi as Commander-in-Chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) and promoted him to the rank of Major General.

In a decree issued on Monday, the Leader, who serves as Commander-in-Chief of the Iranian Armed Forces, cited the “honorable and proud martyrdom” of former IRGC commander Major General Mohammad Pakpour at the hands of the “Zionist-American enemy” as the basis for the appointment, while also recognizing Vahidi’s distinguished service and valuable experience.
​
Ayatollah Khamenei tasked Vahidi with leading the IRGC “under the circumstances that the Islamic establishment is engaged in a strategic and decisive confrontation with global arrogance.”
​
The decree outlined three key priorities for the new IRGC chief:
​
Continuously enhancing comprehensive capabilities to achieve maximum deterrence and maintain smart readiness for powerful offensive operations against enemies;
​
Promoting cultural development within the IRGC and strengthening piety, insight, and revolutionary spirit as the core essence of all commanders and personnel;
​
Expanding management and command structures equipped with strong spiritual and scientific foundations and modern skills throughout the organizational hierarchy.
​
The Leader expressed hope that Iran’s Armed Forces would achieve further successes and consecutive victories.

Long-Term investing strategy

When the crypto market is falling, buying feels scary. When it's going up, it feels like you've already missed your chance.

As a result, most people either buy based on emotion or keep waiting for the perfect entry point — and end up doing nothing at all.

But there's a simple way to avoid this problem: invest a fixed amount of money at regular intervals.

This strategy is called DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging).

You simply choose the asset, the amount you want to invest, and how often you want to buy.

For example:
$50 worth of Bitcoin every week.

When Bitcoin is cheaper, your $50 buys more. When it's more expensive, it buys less. Over time, your average purchase price naturally evens out, and over the course of a few years, it often ends up being better than the average market participant's.

Bybit even has a built-in Auto-Invest bot designed specifically for this strategy. You set it up once — choose your currency, the coin, the investment amount, and the schedule.

After that, your purchases happen automatically, whether it's every day or once a month. The key is to choose a coin you genuinely believe in for the long term.

📌 Transaction Nonces: Why One Stuck Tx Can Block the Next Ones

Main Points
⏺ Wallet transactions are processed in a specific order
⏺ If one transaction gets stuck, later ones may wait behind it
⏺ This post explains why ordering matters and how wallet “traffic jams” happen

1️⃣ What It Is — the network tracks which transaction from an address should come next.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — ordering prevents replay issues and helps the chain process actions correctly.
3️⃣ The Problem — a low-fee transaction can get stuck, blocking later transactions from the same wallet.
4️⃣ User Options — speed it up, replace it, or cancel it with a new transaction using the same nonce.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — don’t fire multiple transactions blindly, and always check fees before signing.

Final Thoughts

In blockchains, the transaction itself matters — but so does its place in line. One weak step can freeze the whole flow after it.
